messages:
customer-techlead: Hey, onboarding our Private agent in a customer VPC and the installer is failing when it tries to pull runtime deps and model shards. Error snippets: "tls: handshake failure" and "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority". Also seeing repeated timeouts to telemetry.redwood.ai. Installer log attached (trimmed).

maria-support: Sorry about the friction — can you paste the exact curl/openssl output for one of the failing hosts and confirm whether you have a corporate TLS intercept/proxy? Also, which installer version are you running?

customer-techlead: Running private-agent-2.4.1. Here's a minimal repro from the host running the installer:

$ curl -v https://files.pythonhosted.org/simple/
* Rebuilt URL to: https://files.pythonhosted.org/simple/
*   Trying 151.101.0.63...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to files.pythonhosted.org (151.101.0.63) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* ALPN, server accepted to use http/1.1
* TLS handshake has read 2311 bytes and written 399 bytes
* SSL: certificate subject: CN=cloudflare, O=Cloudflare, Inc.; issuer: CN=Cloudflare Inc CA
* SSL: certificate issuer: CN=Intercepting-Proxy-CA
* curl: (60) SSL: certificate problem: self signed certificate
* Closing connection 0

And a model shard fetch: 
$ openssl s_client -connect shards-us-west.cdn.redwood.ai:443 -servername shards-us-west.cdn.redwood.ai
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood CA, CN = Redwood Root CA
verify error:num=19: self signed certificate in certificate chain
---

We do have a corporate TLS inspection appliance. We can add certs system-wide but the installer runs in an isolated ephemeral container during bootstrap so it fails before the cert store is populated.

chris-eng: Thanks for the repro — that matches TLS interception breaking the bootstrap. Two paths: (1) allow the installer/container outbound to the Redwood hosts without TLS intercept (transparent passthrough), or (2) pre-inject the interception CA into the installer runtime image/ephemeral container via your image build process. For the quickest unblock, request passthrough to the hostnames below.

infra-bot: KB: https://kb.redwood.ai/private-agent/egress-allowlist — contains a shorter allowlist and curl/openssl checks.

chris-eng: Here's a consolidated allowlist you can present to your network/security team. All entries are HTTPS (443) unless otherwise noted. Where we use wildcards, you can allow the hostname pattern or the specific FQDNs listed. Also, OCSP/CRL checks need outbound access to the CA responders (letsencrypt etc.) — see bottom for OCSP hosts.

Required hostnames (egress outbound):
- files.pythonhosted.org (pip wheels / package index)
- pypi.org, pypi.python.org
- registry.redwood.ai (container images / manifests)
- registry-1.docker.io and auth.docker.io (docker pulls for some images)
- models.redwood.ai and *.models.redwood.ai (model manifests / small metadata endpoints)
- shards-us-*.cdn.redwood.ai (model shard downloads; there are regional buckets: us-west, us-east, eu-central)
- telemetry.redwood.ai (optional, but agent checkout attempts to send usage pings during bootstrap; can be blocked temporarily)
- auth.redwood.ai (OAuth token exchange)
- kms.redwood.ai (optional for KMS-backed keys; 443)
- artifacts.redwood-internal.com (package artifacts for some enterprise builds)
- s3.amazonaws.com and regional S3 endpoints used by shard CDN (if your firewall cannot allow wildcard cdn hostnames)
- time.cloudflare.com / time.google.com (NTP over 123 UDP) — if outbound NTP is strictly blocked, allow NTP or ensure accurate time in the installer image.

Ports: TCP 443 required for TLS. TCP 80 sometimes needed for HTTP->HTTPS redirects for some endpoints during bootstrap. UDP 123 for NTP if you don't pre-sync the host clock.

OCSP/CRL / CA responders (allow for certificate validation):
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org
- ocsp2.globalsign.com
- crl3.digicert.com

Notes about TLS inspection:
- The installer/container must see the original server SNI. If your proxy terminates TLS and re-encrypts with its own cert, you must either:
  * Bypass interception for the hostnames above (recommended for the bootstrap step), OR
  * Inject the corporate interception CA into the ephemeral container image used by the installer (requires rebuilding the image or mounting the host CA into the container runtime).
- OCSP stapling is used for some Redwood endpoints — if your inspection device strips the stapled response the client will fall back to OCSP queries (hence the OCSP hosts above).

Troubleshooting commands (run from the failing host / build agent):
- curl -vS --resolve registry.redwood.ai:443:151.203.40.23 https://registry.redwood.ai/manifest.json\- openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername registry.redwood.ai -showcerts\- python -c "import ssl, socket; print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths())"\- docker pull registry.redwood.ai/agent-bootstrap:2.4.1 (watch for auth errors)

customer-techlead: This is great — thanks. One follow-up: can you give a short list of minimal hosts if our security team will only allow a small set for the initial install?

maria-support: Minimal unblock (bootstrap-only):
- files.pythonhosted.org (443)
- registry.redwood.ai (443)
- shards-us-west.cdn.redwood.ai (443) — pick the region you use
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org (for cert checks)
If you allow just those and ensure TLS passthrough for them, the installer should complete. After install we can relax or reconfigure telemetry if they want to block telemetry.redwood.ai.

chris-eng: If they need IP ranges instead of hostnames, tell us the region(s) used and we can provide S3/CDN prefix lists + Cloud provider ranges for shard delivery. We can also supply a bootstrap tarball that contains wheels and certified images to allow a fully air-gapped install — but that requires a support SLA and a signed request.

customer-techlead: I'll escalate to the security team with this list and the KB link. We'll try passthrough for the minimal set first and report back. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Ping us if they push back on passthrough; we can run a quick remote repro session and provide a temporary narrowed IP set to present to infosec.
